scope.full_target:
A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
correction.

Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
\(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:

1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
   \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
   \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
   assumed.
3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
   \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
   \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).

With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define

\[
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
\qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
\]

The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
\(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.

hypotheses.statement: u:R^n×(0,∞)→R^m is jointly smooth (C^∞ in space and time).
q∈R^m is fixed, independent of space and time, and |q|=1.
For all x∈R^n and all t>0, |u(x,t)|=1.
For each x∈R^n and t>0 there exists a real scalar a such that u_tt(x,t)-Δ_xu(x,t)=a u(x,t). No regularity of a pointwise selection of these scalars is assumed.

binders.type: compact subset of R^n existentially bound for each s,t

hypotheses.statement: For every pair of real numbers 0<s<t<∞ there exists a compact set C_[s,t]⊂R^n such that u(x,r)=q for every x∉C_[s,t] and every r∈[s,t].

source.statement: For every t>0, e(·,t) is Lebesgue integrable on R^n. The finite energy E(t)=∫_{R^n} (|u_t(x,t)|²+∑_{j=1}^n |∂_{x_j}u(x,t)|²) dx is differentiable on (0,∞) and E'(t)=0 for every t>0. In particular E is constant on (0,∞), with exactly this normalization; no assertion at time zero is made.

correspondence.explanation: The full theorem quantifies arbitrary positive dimensions n,m, a jointly smooth map and a single fixed unit vector q with exactly H001–H006. Natural dimension indices subject to H001 are precisely the original positive integer dimensions. The standard coordinates X n with product Lebesgue measure and Euclidean V m identify the original spaces and integrals; Fin n enumerates each original spatial coordinate once. Replacing a map on positive times by an arbitrary real-time extension is reversible by restriction: the positive-time domain is open, so smoothness and every derivative in H005 and the conclusion depend only on the restriction; any source map may be extended arbitrarily outside it. H004 is the original sphere constraint, H005 is pointwise existence of a real normal multiplier with no regularity imposed, and H006 is the same compact perturbation from the fixed q uniformly on each positive closed time interval. The conclusion asserts absolute spatial integrability for every positive time, actual differentiability and derivative zero of the integral of density, and equality of that energy at every pair of positive times. Its norm squares and finite coordinate sum have exactly coefficient one; integrability makes the Bochner scalar integral the ordinary finite Lebesgue integral. No assertion or smooth extension condition is imposed at time zero.
